# Results — Study 242 (Quality-Minus-Junk) on real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — annual sort on
a QMJ composite (profitability + growth + safety pillars), long top quintile (quality) vs
short bottom quintile (junk), equal-weight, one-year reporting lag — measured against the
equal-weight universe on the current S&P 500 universe projected backwards. As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| QMJ composite score | 16 years × 411 tickers | `cad0237edf69` |
| Forward returns | 16 years × 420 tickers | `2d5ea197105a` |
| Years covered | 2010 – 2025 | — |

**Sources:** EDGAR XBRL shared caches (`_edgar_GrossProfit.parquet`, `_edgar_Assets.parquet`,
`_edgar_NetIncomeLoss.parquet`, `_edgar_Revenues.parquet`, `_edgar_StockholdersEquity.parquet`,
`_edgar_NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities.parquet`); annual returns from
`_edgar_yrret.parquet` (Yahoo Finance monthly prices, calendar-year compounded). Universe:
current S&P 500 membership, survivorship-biased. Signal years with fewer than 30 firms are
dropped; 2026 (partial) is excluded.

**QMJ pillars:**
- **Profitability** — equal-weight z-score of GP/A, ROA, net-margin, CFO/Assets
- **Growth** — year-over-year change in the profitability composite (z-scored)
- **Safety** — equity / assets (low-leverage proxy, z-scored)
- *Payout excluded* — no dividend/share-count cache in the shared EDGAR store

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the universe is the current S&P 500 membership
projected backwards. All positive results should be read as **upper-bound estimates**;
the true population effect is likely smaller and possibly absent.

## The honest test — quality vs junk quintile, annual rebalance

Signal in year *y* = QMJ composite built from fiscal year-*y* EDGAR filings. Strategy
enters at Jan 1 of year *y+1* (after full reporting delay) and measures the return during
calendar year *y+1*.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N years | 16 (2010–2025) |
| Mean hedge return | **+2.71%/yr** |
| Vol | 15.04%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | +0.180 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.907** |
| Hit rate (years > 0) | 50.0% |
| Max drawdown | −26.0% |

- The hedge earns **+2.71%/yr** at HAC *t* = **+0.907** — well below the inference bar of
  |*t*| ≥ 2. The effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero at conventional levels.
- The quality leg earns **+23.0%/yr** vs the equal-weight market at **+19.0%/yr** —
  the quality leg outperforms the market by **+4.0%/yr** on this survivor panel.
- The junk leg earns **+20.3%/yr**, outperforming the market by **+1.3%/yr**.
- Hit rate is exactly 50% (8/16 years positive); the most recent two years (2024, 2025)
  were both negative (−9.5%, −17.1%), consistent with quality-factor crowding and reversal.

## Legs vs equal-weight market

| Leg | Mean return | vs market |
|---|--:|--:|
| Quality (top quintile QMJ) | +23.0%/yr | +4.0%/yr |
| Junk (bottom quintile QMJ) | +20.3%/yr | +1.3%/yr |
| **Hedge (quality − junk)** | **+2.71%/yr** | — |
| Equal-weight market | +19.0%/yr | 0 |

Note: both legs outperform the equal-weight market on the survivorship-biased panel, but
the *spread* between quality and junk is small and noisy (HAC t < 1).

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Hedge HAC *t* = +0.907 (|t| < 2). The mean (+2.71%/yr) is positive
  and consistent with the AQR QMJ literature on broad universes, but falls below the
  inference bar on this short, large-cap, survivorship-biased panel. Strong academic prior
  (Asness et al. 2019) upgrades from NONE to WEAK, but real-tape numbers alone do not
  clear the bar.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Sharpe +0.180, hit rate 50%, max drawdown −26.0%, and
  the most recent two years both reversed sharply. The large-cap survivor universe lacks
  the cross-sectional dispersion needed for a robust hedge; the Payout pillar is also
  absent here. A full, broad-universe QMJ implementation (Russell 3000, Payout included)
  would be needed to assess true tradability.
- **Survivorship caveat:** the current S&P 500 panel biases the quality leg upward (quality
  firms are disproportionately represented in survivors). The junk short candidates may
  have been delisted before appearing in the sample.
